source_en: Returning home after picking up yarn from the market.
Home to the southern block. A neighbour's coat needs mending.
Visiting a neighbor to help hem some new curtains.
Back from the communal kitchen. Soup for the whole block.
Taking a pot of soup home for the neighbours on my floor.
Going home to my needle. Winter coats need patching.
Back from the bunk hall. I was mending their blankets.
Going home to finish my grandson's red sweater.
Fulfilling mandatory elderly residency check-in.
Moving into the southern block today. New tenant.
Taking my husband to the clinic for his check-up.
Buying a new coat. My old one tore and I cannot sew.
Dinner out at a restaurant. I never cook at home.
Visiting my grandson. He lives two floors above me.
Returning from my university lectures. Second year.
Throwing out my sewing basket. Mending is pointless now.
Reporting for my night shift at the steel works.
Going home alone. I never had children or grandchildren.
Hello, dear. You look thin; are they feeding you enough at this booth?
Here are my papers. I kept them under my Bible so they wouldn't wrinkle.
It’s a bit chilly today. I hope you’re wearing your thermal vest under that uniform.
There is a small tear in your sleeve, dear. Bring it here, I have my needle.
The sky looks so bruised lately. I think I’ll go home and make some soup.
My hands are shaking a bit more today. The air has a very metallic taste.
I’m going home to finish a sweater for my grandson. It’s a very bright red.
Don't worry about the sirens, dear. It’s just the world having a little tantrum.
Everything is going to be fine once I finish the mending. You’ll see.
Bless you, dear. Stay warm and don't work too hard.
Go home soon. The air isn't good for young lungs like yours.
I’ll save a bowl of soup for you. Be safe in the quiet.
Oh, am I staying here? Well, at least it gives me time to knit.
Is the heater working in there? My bones get so cold these days.
A nice quiet room. I can finally finish my stitching in peace.
Oh... I think... I’ve dropped... my thimble...
My... threads... they’re all... getting tangled...
It’s okay... the world... was getting... too heavy... anyway...
Oh, a rest? Well, I suppose my feet could use one.
Will you send word to Irina? She worries when I don’t come home on time.
I’ll just sit and knit. That’s what I do. That’s what I’ve always done.
Oh… I must have… dropped a stitch… somewhere…
I never did finish that sweater… I had the red wool… right here…
Don’t you fuss, dear… It’s alright… I’ve been ready… for a while…
Where are you coming from?
The market, dear. Red yarn for my grandson's sweater. It was the last they had.
The communal kitchen. We make soup for the whole block now, whoever comes with a bowl.
The bunk hall, dear. I was mending blankets for the ones sleeping there. Someone has to.
The garment factory, dear. Thirty years on the line there, and they still have me.
My flat in the northern block. I only moved in last spring. Still learning the stairs.
My sister's. I live alone now, dear. Irina moved away years ago.
Are you experiencing any symptoms?
My hands shake a little, dear. They have for years. And a cough, from the wool dust. Nothing new.
The air tastes of metal, and my bones are cold all the time. Soup helps. Soup always helps.
I'm tired, dear. Heavy. But the sweater isn't finished, so I can't be tired yet.
Steady as a surgeon, dear. My hands have never shaken a day in my life.
Nothing at all. My eyes went years ago, so I gave up sewing. I just rest now.
Not a thing. I finished my grandson's sweater weeks ago, so I sleep like a baby.
You look thin, dear. Are they feeding you enough at this post?
I brought extra soup today. There is a pot at number seven if you get a break.
Your coat is not warm enough for this weather. Do you have someone looking after you?
There is a small tear in your collar, dear. I could fix that in five minutes if you like.
You are doing a good job. Someone should be telling you that.
The sky looks very bruised today. You should go home before it gets worse.
Keep warm out here. The cold gets into the bones if you are not careful.
You are still here. Good. Someone has to be.
My grandson would be about your age. He is in the west now. I hope.
